newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * The opposition Party of Social Democracy lodged a no-confidence motion in parliament on Thursday against the government's failure to meet its electoral promises.
The motion was signed by 140 opposition MPs.

* Parliament's upper chamber, the Senate, has passed a government decree on social security measures for employees who lose their jobs as a result of restructuring and liquidation of state-run companies.

Under the bill employees can get up to 12 average monthly wages -- in monthly payments -- depending on their length of service. They can get the whole amount at one go if they start their own small business.
Employees launching their own businesses will be exempt from taxes, the bill says.
* The lower Chamber of Deputies voted a bill increasing to 200 hectares from 100 hectares the land area which one family can own.
The bill also says foreign citizens cannot own land, but allows Romanian citizens living abroad to buy land in Romania.

* The Romanian-Ukrainian friendship treaty is a vital document for bilateral relations and for Romania's chances to join NATO in a first wave of the alliance's expansion, said Dumitru Ceausu, Foreign Ministry Secretary of State.

* Romanian Integration Minister Alexandru Herlea and the European Community's representative to Bucharest, Karen Fogg, signed a memorandum on Thursday on the co-financing of a project to upgrade water supplies in the coalmining Jiu Valley region.
Under the memorandum, some 18 percent of the cost of the project (or 8.4 million Ecus) will be covered from PHARE funds.
* The state will only be able to purchase a quarter of this year's wheat output for national reserves, said deputy Trita Fanita, head of parliament farming commission.
He warned that the government and the central bank would have to find ways to finance the purchase of the rest of the crop.
